title: A Oath for the Wolf
premise: Hazel Okonkwo, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who has not spoken in a decade, is forced to accept a dying stranger's map — which turns out to be the key to the Thornfell's oldest prison. The 'king' of Thornfell has been hollowed out and worn like armor by an ancient wolf-spirit that feeds on memory, erasing whole villages from history to grow stronger. Hazel discovers her silent god did not abandon her: it was devoured first, and she carries its last surviving fragment in her own forgotten past. To free the king, she must surrender her memories — including her identity as the woman named Hazel — but she finds a third path: binding the wolf with her living oath rather than her dead past, at the cost of never hearing any god again. In the end the king wakes, the wolf is chained beneath the mountain, and Hazel walks out of Thornfell nameless but unbroken, choosing who she will be.
about_author: Hazel Thackeray is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through remote mountain passes before turning to fantasy fiction. She writes stories about oaths, wild places, and the price of remembering.

chapters.title: The Silent Altar
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. On a smuggler's run through Thornfell, Hazel makes her nightly offering to her silent god and gets nothing back, as always. A rival crew mocks her faith; she nearly starts a fight over it. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence — she is good at her work precisely because she expects nothing from anyone, even heaven.

chapters.title: Blood on the Map
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. A stranger stumbles into her camp, gut-wounded, and presses a leather map into her hands with a dying command: 'Don't let him finish the count.' He names her — a name she doesn't recognize — before dying. Emotional beat: dread and curiosity colliding; the map burns cold against her skin, and she cannot bring herself to sell it.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Following the map, Hazel finds villages that appear on no ledger, where locals greet her by name and forget her within minutes. She realizes memories are being harvested here. Emotional beat: creeping horror — the competent loner confronts a threat that attacks the one thing she's built her life on: knowing the roads.

chapters.title: The Court of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Summoned to the capital, Hazel meets King Aldric, whose eyes flicker between warmth and something ancient and hungry. His advisor, Lady Vess, quietly warns her: the man you saw is real; the thing wearing his crown counts memories like coins. Emotional beat: political unease sharpening into moral stakes.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Ate
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess reveals the history: centuries ago the wolf-god Fenmar was bound under Thornfell, and the royal line renewed the binding with sacrifice until Aldric's greed broke the rite. Fenmar escaped into the king and now eats memory to grow. Emotional beat: grief for a slow-motion catastrophe, and guilt — Vess helped break it.

chapters.title: A Name I Never Gave
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The dying stranger's word for her resurfaces: she was once a temple acolyte of Fenmar's rival god, her memories stolen when the god went silent. Her oath wasn't abandoned — it was swallowed. Emotional beat: identity crisis; everything she believed about herself was a survivor's blank page.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Nine
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Fenmar, aware of her, offers a bargain: serve him and he'll return her stolen past whole. Meanwhile his forces seize the mountain shrines, and the ninth binding-stone falls. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive — he shows her a childhood she aches for, and it may be real.

chapters.title: Oathbreaker's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess sacrifices herself smuggling Hazel into the deep vaults, buying time with her own memories until she forgets why she's helping. Emotional beat: tragic devotion — redemption purchased with self-erasure, showing Hazel exactly what surrendering memory costs.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. In the vault beneath the crown, Hazel reaches the fragment of her dead god inside Fenmar and refuses both bargains: she re-swears her original oath aloud, using her living vow — not lost memories — as the new chain. Fenmar is dragged back under the mountain; Aldric collapses, freed but broken. Emotional beat: climax — fierce, costly triumph.

chapters.title: Nameless on the High Road
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The king, diminished, begins rebuilding honest bindings; the forgotten villages slowly remember themselves. Hazel, her old name returned but her god still gone, walks out of Thornfell toward an unwritten future. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — identity is not what was taken from you, but what you choose next.
